nodes.label: Composite Index Ordering Rule
nodes.rationale: When queries filter on multiple columns, a composite index is more efficient than separate single-column indexes. Equality columns must precede range columns due to the leftmost prefix rule.

nodes.label: WHERE and JOIN Column Indexing Rule
nodes.norm_label: where and join column indexing rule
nodes.rationale: Unindexed columns in WHERE and JOIN clauses cause sequential table scans. For JOIN columns, always index the referencing foreign key column.

nodes.label: Foreign Key Indexing Pattern
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not automatically index foreign keys; missing FK indexes cause slow JOINs and table-locking full scans during ON DELETE CASCADE operations.

nodes.label: Lowercase Snake Case Identifier Convention
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase. Quoted mixed-case identifiers require quoting in every query and break compatibility with ORMs, tools, and AI assistants.

nodes.label: 100% Free Hosting Architecture
nodes.rationale: ScrumTool is designed to be hosted permanently for $0/month on Vercel's Hobby tier with a Supabase PostgreSQL free-tier database.

nodes.label: Anti-Exploit and Tamper Protections
nodes.rationale: Enforces server-side gate checks, constant-time HMAC admin session authentication, CSV formula sanitization (=, +, -, @ prefix quoting), and strict 0-24 hour range validation.

nodes.label: Domain Edge Cases (Joined Date, Leave/PTO, Timezone, Future Dates)
nodes.norm_label: domain edge cases (joined date, leave/pto, timezone, future dates)
nodes.rationale: Resolves new hire onboarding by bounding gate checks to joined_at, auto-satisfies PTO days with 0 hours, transmits dates in local browser timezone, and rejects future dates beyond 1 day.

nodes.label: Decimal Hours and Zero Hour Logging Rule
nodes.norm_label: decimal hours and zero hour logging rule
nodes.rationale: Supports standard floats (0.25, 0.5, 1.5) and explicitly permits 0.00 hours to denote planned tasks that were postponed without blocking the member.

nodes.label: Idempotency via Deterministic Client UUIDs and UPSERT
nodes.norm_label: idempotency via deterministic client uuids and upsert
nodes.rationale: Client generates deterministic UUIDv4s before network transmission and server executes UPSERT on task IDs and daily submissions to guarantee zero duplicates even under flaky connections.

nodes.label: Missing Hours Gate and Standup Eligibility
nodes.norm_label: missing hours gate and standup eligibility
nodes.rationale: Prevents a team member from creating or editing tasks for today if there is any past working day where tasks exist with unentered or unlocked hours, skipping weekends and registered company holidays.

nodes.label: Post-Submission Immutability (Locking)
nodes.rationale: Once a member locks their day, records are permanently immutable from the client interface, with unlock operations restricted exclusively to administrative overrides.

nodes.label: Batch INSERT and COPY Bulk Loading Rule
nodes.norm_label: batch insert and copy bulk loading rule
nodes.rationale: Individual single-row INSERT statements incur severe round-trip network latency and per-statement transaction overhead. Batching up to ~1000 rows in single multi-row VALUES statements or streaming with COPY delivers 10-50x faster bulk ingestion.

nodes.label: N+1 Query Elimination with Batch Loading Rule
nodes.norm_label: n+1 query elimination with batch loading rule
nodes.rationale: Querying related child rows iteratively inside an application loop generates N+1 round trips to the database. Replacing the loop with ANY(array) filtering or SQL JOINs consolidates operations into a single round trip.

nodes.label: Cursor Keyset Pagination vs OFFSET Rule
nodes.norm_label: cursor keyset pagination vs offset rule
nodes.rationale: OFFSET pagination scans and discards all preceding rows, resulting in O(N) performance that degrades on deep pages. Keyset pagination using indexed WHERE filters (e.g. id > last_id) guarantees constant O(1) performance at arbitrary page depth.

nodes.label: Atomic UPSERT with ON CONFLICT Rule
nodes.norm_label: atomic upsert with on conflict rule
nodes.rationale: Separate SELECT-then-INSERT/UPDATE logic causes race conditions when concurrent requests check simultaneously, resulting in duplicate key constraint violations. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE provides atomic insert-or-update without locks.

nodes.norm_label: skip locked queue processing reference guide

nodes.label: PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED Documentation
nodes.norm_label: postgresql select for update skip locked documentation

nodes.label: Application Advisory Locks Rule
nodes.rationale: Creating synthetic table rows for application concurrency coordination incurs table bloat and lock overhead. Advisory locks (pg_advisory_lock, pg_advisory_xact_lock, pg_try_advisory_lock) coordinate distributed application processes purely in-memory.

nodes.label: Consistent Lock Ordering Deadlock Prevention Rule
nodes.norm_label: consistent lock ordering deadlock prevention rule
nodes.rationale: Deadlocks happen when concurrent transactions acquire locks in inconsistent orders. Ensuring all transactions acquire resources in a strict, predictable order (e.g. sorted primary keys) or using atomic multi-row updates prevents circular lock waits.

nodes.label: Minimal Transaction Scope and Timeout Rule
nodes.norm_label: minimal transaction scope and timeout rule
nodes.rationale: Long-running transactions hold locks that stall other transactions and increase deadlock risk, especially when external HTTP or payment API calls take place within the transaction. Restrict transactions strictly to database operations and enforce statement_timeout.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED Non-Blocking Worker Queue Rule
nodes.norm_label: skip locked non-blocking worker queue rule
nodes.rationale: Workers selecting jobs with standard FOR UPDATE block each other on the top pending row. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED bypasses locked rows instantly, granting each worker the next available item for 10x parallel queue throughput.

nodes.label: Execution Plan Bottleneck Identification
nodes.rationale: Examines Seq Scan on large tables for missing indexes, high Rows Removed by Filter for poor selectivity, buffer read >> hit for low memory, and external merge sorts for work_mem bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Query Diagnostics with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: Executes queries to measure actual execution timings and buffer cache hits vs reads, revealing actual performance bottlenecks like sequential scans and memory spills rather than guessing.

nodes.label: High-Latency Query Optimization Strategy
nodes.rationale: Focuses optimization on queries where mean_exec_time > 100ms or calls are highest to maximize throughput and reduce database load.

nodes.label: Query Execution Statistics Tracking
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements records execution statistics for all queries across the database, allowing identification of slowest queries by total execution time, mean execution latency, and frequency.

nodes.label: High-Churn Autovacuum Tuning
nodes.rationale: Tightening autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor (e.g. 0.05) and autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor (e.g. 0.02) triggers vacuum and analyze much earlier on busy tables to prevent dead tuple bloat.

nodes.label: Table Statistics Maintenance via ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: Stale planner statistics cause the query optimizer to miscalculate row estimates and choose sequential scans instead of index scans; running ANALYZE restores accurate plans (2-10x improvement).

nodes.label: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle connections waste resources and hold locks; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout reclaim 30-50% connection slots

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.rationale: Too many connections exhaust RAM (1-3MB per connection) and cause crashes; calculate max_connections based on available RAM and tune work_mem

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications
nodes.rationale: Postgres connections are expensive; connection poolers like PgBouncer allow 10-100x more concurrent users via transaction or session pooling

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are tied to individual connections; in transaction pooling they cause missing statement errors unless unnamed statements or session pooling is used

nodes.label: Row Level Security Multi-Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Row Level Security enforces data boundary at the database engine level, preventing cross-tenant leaks even if application code is bypassed or contains filtering bugs. Requires alter table force row level security.

nodes.label: RLS Subquery Wrapping and Security Definer Pattern
nodes.norm_label: rls subquery wrapping and security definer pattern
nodes.rationale: Wrap auth.uid() inside a scalar subquery (select auth.uid()) so PostgreSQL evaluates and caches it once per query instead of per row; use SECURITY DEFINER helper functions in private schemas with explicit search_path for complex multi-table checks.

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking
nodes.rationale: Creating dummy database rows for locks adds table bloat and overhead; pg_advisory_lock and pg_advisory_xact_lock provide lightweight application coordination

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering
nodes.rationale: Transactions locking resources in different orders cause deadlocks; always acquire row locks in deterministic ID order with SELECT FOR UPDATE or atomic updates

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention
nodes.rationale: Long-running transactions hold locks that block other queries; execute external API calls and validations outside transactions and set statement_timeout

nodes.label: Composite Index Column Ordering Rule
nodes.rationale: When queries filter on multiple columns, a composite index avoids slower bitmap index scans. Equality columns must be placed first and range columns last to respect leftmost prefix matching.

nodes.label: Covering Index with INCLUDE Clause
nodes.rationale: Covering indexes append selected non-filtered columns via the INCLUDE clause, enabling index-only scans that eliminate table heap fetches and yield 2-5x faster query execution.

nodes.label: Index Type Selection (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash)
nodes.norm_label: index type selection (b-tree, gin, gist, brin, hash)
nodes.rationale: Selecting the correct index type (GIN for JSONB/arrays, GiST for geometry/KNN, BRIN for large time-series, Hash for equality, B-tree for general range/equality) provides 10-100x improvement over default B-tree.

nodes.label: Range Partitioning for Time-Series Data
nodes.rationale: Partitioning tables with >100M rows by date range isolates query scans to relevant partitions and allows instant data purging via DROP TABLE instead of long-running DELETE statements.

nodes.label: WHERE and JOIN Column Indexing Guide
nodes.norm_label: where and join column indexing guide

nodes.label: WHERE and JOIN Predicate Indexing Rule
nodes.norm_label: where and join predicate indexing rule
nodes.rationale: Queries filtering or joining on unindexed columns cause full table sequential scans that degrade exponentially as tables grow; indexing frequently filtered and referencing foreign key columns makes queries 100-1000x faster.

nodes.label: Foreign Key Indexing for JOINs and Cascades
nodes.norm_label: foreign key indexing for joins and cascades
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not auto-index foreign keys; without an index, ON DELETE CASCADE and joins trigger full table sequential scans and table locks, resulting in 10-100x performance penalties.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Data Types Best Practices Guide
nodes.norm_label: postgresql data types best practices guide

nodes.label: Optimal Data Type Selection
nodes.rationale: Selecting bigint over int prevents overflow; text over varchar(n) avoids arbitrary limits without performance penalty; timestamptz stores timezone context; numeric preserves exact monetary decimal precision.

nodes.label: Optimal Primary Key Strategy (Identity vs UUIDv7)
nodes.norm_label: optimal primary key strategy (identity vs uuidv7)
nodes.rationale: Use bigint generated always as identity for single databases; for distributed systems use time-ordered UUIDv7 or ULID to prevent B-tree index fragmentation caused by random UUIDv4.

nodes.label: Use tsvector for Full-Text Search
nodes.rationale: LIKE with wildcards cannot use standard indexes and causes full table scans; tsvector with GIN indexing delivers 100x faster searches and relevance ranking

nodes.label: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
nodes.norm_label: index jsonb columns for efficient querying
nodes.rationale: JSONB queries without indexes scan entire tables; GIN indexes with jsonb_ops or jsonb_path_ops accelerate containment queries 10-100x

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data
nodes.rationale: Individual inserts cause high round-trip overhead; multi-row INSERT or COPY achieves 10-50x faster bulk loading

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading
nodes.rationale: N+1 queries execute one query per item in a loop; batch loading via ANY(array[...]) or JOINs eliminates 10-100x round trips

nodes.label: Covering Index with INCLUDE Clause
nodes.rationale: Covering indexes include all columns needed by a query using the INCLUDE clause, enabling index-only scans that skip table heap lookups entirely.

nodes.label: Index Type Selection (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash)
nodes.norm_label: index type selection (b-tree, gin, gist, brin, hash)
nodes.rationale: Different index types excel at different query patterns: B-tree for range/equality comparisons, GIN for JSONB and arrays, GiST for geometric/ranges, BRIN for large time-series, Hash for equality-only.

nodes.label: Partial Index Optimization Rule
nodes.rationale: Partial indexes only include rows matching a WHERE condition, making them 5-20x smaller and speeding up writes and queries when filtering on subset conditions like soft-deletes or pending statuses.

nodes.label: Idempotent Constraint Creation via DO Block
nodes.norm_label: idempotent constraint creation via do block
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; migrations must inspect pg_constraint inside a DO block before adding constraints to enable idempotent schema changes.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Data Type Selection Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Using appropriate data types reduces storage by 50% and improves comparisons: bigint for identity IDs, text over varchar(n), timestamptz for timestamps, numeric for financial values, and boolean flags.

nodes.label: Range Partitioning for Large Tables
nodes.rationale: Partitioning splits large tables (>100M rows) by time ranges, accelerating queries via partition pruning and allowing instant table drops instead of costly DELETE operations.

nodes.label: Optimal Primary Key Selection Strategy
nodes.rationale: Use bigint generated always as identity for single databases (SQL standard, compact 8 bytes); use UUIDv7 or ULID for distributed systems to avoid B-tree index fragmentation from random UUIDv4.

nodes.label: Least Privilege Database Roles Strategy
nodes.rationale: Never connect applications via superuser. Enforce least privilege with non-login roles (e.g. app_readonly, app_writer), revoke default public schema grants, and grant scoped SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE permissions.

nodes.label: Partial Index Optimization Rule
nodes.rationale: Partial indexes include only rows matching a common WHERE filter (such as active records or pending orders), producing 5-20x smaller indexes that consume less memory and lower insert/update overhead.

nodes.label: Lowercase Snake_Case Identifiers Convention
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase. Quoted mixed-case identifiers require persistent quoting and cause subtle case-sensitivity bugs across ORMs, tools, and AI assistants.

nodes.rationale: Added schema constraints reference for safe non-blocking migration patterns

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset
nodes.rationale: OFFSET pagination scans and discards preceding rows; keyset cursor pagination maintains O(1) indexed query time regardless of page depth

nodes.label: tsvector Full-Text Search with GIN Indexing Rule
nodes.norm_label: tsvector full-text search with gin indexing rule
nodes.rationale: LIKE wildcards cannot use standard B-tree indexes, forcing full table scans. Stored generated tsvector columns indexed with GIN deliver 100x faster searches, supporting boolean query operators and ts_rank relevance scoring.

nodes.label: JSONB GIN and Expression Indexing Rule
nodes.norm_label: jsonb gin and expression indexing rule
nodes.rationale: Unindexed JSONB containment queries scan entire tables. GIN indexes accelerate @> containment queries. jsonb_path_ops yields 2-3x smaller indexes when containment is the only operator needed, while expression indexes optimize specific scalar path lookups.

nodes.label: Idle Connection Timeouts Configuration Rule
nodes.rationale: Idle client connections hold memory and transaction locks indefinitely. Configuring idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (30s) and idle_session_timeout (10min) reclaims 30-50% of connection slots from stalled clients.

nodes.label: Connection Limits & Memory Budgeting Rule
nodes.rationale: Each connection consumes 1-3MB RAM. Blindly raising max_connections causes memory exhaustion and crashes. Tune max_connections (100-200) and set work_mem such that max_connections * work_mem <= 25% of total system RAM.

nodes.label: Connection Pooling & Sizing Rule
nodes.rationale: Direct connections per client request crash databases under high concurrent user load. Utilizing a connection pooler like PgBouncer multiplexes 10-100x more client traffic over a compact connection pool sized according to CPU cores and I/O capacity.

nodes.label: Prepared Statements in Pooled Environments Rule
nodes.norm_label: prepared statements in pooled environments rule
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are bound to individual server connections. Under transaction-mode pooling where connections are shared across different clients, named statements collide. Use unnamed prepared statements, deallocate after use, or use session-mode pooling.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE Query Profiling Rule
nodes.rationale: Diagnosing slow queries by intuition misses underlying causes. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) runs the query, highlighting actual execution timings, filter selectivity, disk reads vs buffer cache hits, and expensive join algorithms.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements Query Performance Tracking Rule
nodes.rationale: Optimizing individual queries requires knowing which queries consume the most database resources. pg_stat_statements aggregates execution count, total runtime, and mean latency across all queries to pinpoint optimization targets.

nodes.label: VACUUM and ANALYZE Table Statistics Rule
nodes.norm_label: vacuum and analyze table statistics rule
nodes.rationale: Stale planner statistics cause the query planner to choose sequential scans instead of index scans. Regular ANALYZE maintains fresh distribution statistics, VACUUM reclaims dead tuples, and lowering autovacuum scale factors prevents degradation on high-write tables.

nodes.label: Use UPSERT for Insert-or-Update Operations
nodes.rationale: SELECT-then-INSERT/UPDATE creates race conditions; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE/NOTHING provides atomic, concurrency-safe upserts

nodes.label: Atomic Queue Claim-and-Update Pattern
nodes.rationale: Combines SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside an UPDATE statement with RETURNING * to claim and advance job state atomically in a single statement without race conditions.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED Non-Blocking Worker Queue Pattern
nodes.norm_label: skip locked non-blocking worker queue pattern
nodes.rationale: When multiple worker processes consume a queue table, SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED bypasses currently locked rows without waiting, eliminating worker contention and yielding 10x throughput.

nodes.label: Idempotent Constraint Creation via DO Blocks
nodes.norm_label: idempotent constraint creation via do blocks
nodes.rationale: Because PostgreSQL does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS, wrapping ALTER TABLE in a DO block checking pg_constraint ensures safe, idempotent migration reruns.

nodes.label: Least Privilege Role Segregation
nodes.rationale: Segregating application database access into minimal nologin roles (app_readonly, app_writer) and revoking public defaults limits the attack surface and blast radius of SQL injection.

nodes.label: Database-Enforced Tenant Isolation via RLS
nodes.rationale: Row Level Security enforces data access boundaries at the database engine level, preventing catastrophic data leaks caused by application bugs or query parameter bypasses.

nodes.label: Controlled Security Definer Function Pattern
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER functions bypass RLS for complex team or membership lookups, but must include explicit auth.uid() checks, fixed search_path = '', and revoked public execution to avoid privilege escalation.

nodes.label: Subquery Function Wrapping in RLS Policies
nodes.norm_label: subquery function wrapping in rls policies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping auth functions in a SELECT subquery ((select auth.uid()) = user_id) evaluates and caches the result once per query rather than once per row, running 100x+ faster on large tables.
